mbm-1676.quote: We lost a game's wooden counters and borrowed raisins from the kitchen. By the last round Mum's ginger biscuits had swallowed both armies. We finished by counting crumbs.

mbm-1677.clue: I don't lend out the blue towel.
mbm-1677.quote: After my first water-ski start I came aboard dripping and grinning. My uncle wrapped me in a towel with huge blue fish. I keep it at the dock for anybody who stands up for the first time.

mbm-1678.quote: I drilled pinholes into the cardboard hangar behind my model robot and put a little lamp outside it. At bedtime the hangar has a sky full of stars. I nearly forgot to paint the robot.

mbm-1679.clue: We call that corner the orchestra pit.
mbm-1679.quote: One side of our beach court runs along a low wooden boardwalk. When a hard serve bounces off it, the planks play a different note. Our longest rally sounded almost tuneful.

mbm-1680.clue: I mark the ball with a little open umbrella.
mbm-1680.quote: I learned to putt in a hallway on rainy days. We set a mug by the skirting board and tried to tap it gently with the ball. I still draw a little umbrella on each ball to remind me of the rain and that first clean ping.

mbm-1681.clue: My pajamas have a seat reserved.
mbm-1681.quote: Everyone in my family has a favorite sofa spot for the Friday show. One night I came in late and found my flannel top arranged on my cushion, sleeves folded exactly the way I sit.

mbm-1682.clue: I know my friend's stroke by its splash.
mbm-1682.quote: At the municipal pool we can't talk from opposite lanes. We invented a greeting with two quick splashes at the wall. Even with my goggles off, I know who's arrived.

mbm-1683.clue: I draw my best monster on the train.
mbm-1683.quote: On the ride home from anime club we pass two water towers and a power pole. For half a second their shadows look like a giant robot. I filled six sketchbook pages trying to catch its knees.

mbm-1684.clue: I put a receipt under my shoelace.
mbm-1684.quote: The lady at the fruit stall bet I'd run my hill before she sold her last pear. I got back while she was wrapping it and she wrote my time on the receipt. Fastest pear I've ever eaten.

mbm-1685.clue: The heron gets first choice of seats.
mbm-1685.quote: A heron claimed the overturned canoe on the bank. I waited for it to leave while I drank my tea. It waited for the sun. That was the first time I ever took a boat out at noon.

mbm-1686.clue: We give the last chair a silent salute.
mbm-1686.quote: My oldest ski photograph shows Dad on a lift with a powdery white eyebrow. Last season snow fell on me in exactly the same spot. My daughter held both photos up and couldn't stop laughing.

mbm-1687.clue: I can pitch our tent with my eyes shut now.
mbm-1687.quote: We camped in the backyard and my cousin forgot the poles. We tied the tent over the clothesline. By morning every towel peg wore a tiny cap of dew.

mbm-1688.clue: I painted the hole with the door open.
mbm-1688.quote: Our community center wanted a mural around the old keyhole. I gave it a tiny lighthouse and kept the handle for a pier. Turn the key when the sun's behind the door and the lighthouse flashes.

mbm-1689.clue: On this map the cave is shaped like a cake.
mbm-1689.quote: At my hiking group's birthday walk we cooled a cake in a shady hollow. Our newest member drew a little slice on the trail map. People have been bringing forks ever since.

mbm-1690.clue: I give my clay birds one heavy foot.
mbm-1690.quote: I sculpted a little robin to hold down the newspaper. Its tail lifted in the breeze, so I added a generous lump of clay to one foot. Now it looks ready to stamp on the crossword.

mbm-1691.clue: I found the pit that beat me.
mbm-1691.quote: At the mango-eating contest a stubborn bit of fruit clung to the pit through the final bell. I pointed to it when the judge came by. She awarded the last point to the mango, and our table applauded.

mbm-1692.clue: My favorite bird doesn't appear in the drawing.
mbm-1692.quote: A wren sat on my field guide while I sketched a whole hedge looking for it. My friend took a picture of us. I'm still holding my pencil in midair and the wren looks quite pleased.

mbm-1693.clue: I bring a spoon to the pirate hole.
mbm-1693.quote: The pirate ship on our mini golf course collects rain. We keep a big spoon under the bench to bail it out for the next group. Some days I spend longer saving the ship than putting.

mbm-1694.clue: I let the bookshop cat choose Tuesdays.
mbm-1694.quote: The shop cat blocks one shelf every Tuesday afternoon. I borrow whichever book she leaves her tail on. Last week I learned more about shipbuilding than either of us expected.

mbm-1695.clue: I leave one corner of the page blank for a hat.
mbm-1695.quote: The conductor of my favorite morning train always waves his cap at the footbridge. I draw the engine first and wait with my red pencil ready for the little flash in the cab.

mbm-1696.clue: I traded my best dance move for a shoelace.
mbm-1696.quote: My shoe came loose halfway across a crowded floor. A stranger handed me a spare purple lace and asked how to do the side step. We were both ready for the next record.

mbm-1697.clue: My strongest card carries a teacup.
mbm-1697.quote: I gave my dragon deck a tiny tea trolley made from a matchbox. I wheel it out when a game runs long. The younger players wave the dragons into line and order hot chocolate.

mbm-1698.clue: I take photographs of the shadows underneath things.
mbm-1698.quote: Everyone crowded around the fountain to see the stone lions. Across the square their long shadows were drinking from a gutter. That was the picture I put on my wall.

mbm-1699.clue: I know the show from its ad breaks.
mbm-1699.quote: Our family acts out the missing scene during commercials. It's a house rule that whoever's in striped pajamas plays the mayor. I bought two striped pairs for election season.

mbm-1700.clue: I've got half a rainbow in my tackle box.
mbm-1700.quote: I glued the colored scraps from repairing my kayak in a little row inside the lid. From blue scrape to yellow scrape, that's three summers of rocky landings in one box.
